sections.heading: DOES IRUMA THINK IN WRITTEN OR SPOKEN JAPANESE?
sections.content:
Q: I want to ask something a little strange. When Iruma-sensei is thinking things through in his head, does he use written-style language, or spoken-style language? I always assumed I thought in written style myself, but today I realized it had switched to spoken style.

A: Spoken style, definitely. Thinking in written style would be exhausting.

sections.heading: A WORD FOR EXAM-TAKERS
sections.content:
Q: I'm a student taking exams right now — could you give me a word of encouragement?

A: It's a pretty ordinary thing to say, but: hang in there! The experience of pushing through something hard will pay off eventually.

sections.heading: WHEN TO SAY "JUST KIDDING"
sections.content:
Q: Actually, the first sound in my name is also "Mi," so I guess that makes me a Mii-kun too. Yay! But I don't really understand the right timing or method for using the phrase "just kidding." Should I say it quietly, or just think it to myself? If you have any tips, please share them!

A: You mustn't lie to people!

sections.heading: THE NUMBERED CHAPTERS OF THE ISOLATED
sections.content:
Q: I finished reading The Isolated. When I finally understood the meaning behind the numbers listed in the chapter titles, I genuinely had an "aha" moment.[ref:koritsusha] The fact that leap years were factored in too is genuinely impressive. By the way, this is a bit of a tangent, but I'd really love to read the "Multiple Personality, Roughly Saitou" mentioned in the afterword.[ref:saitou-afterword] I'm looking forward to this one getting a print release!

A: Ah, that thing again… I've got a rough idea for the story worked out, so let me think about how to actually write it once things settle down. Also, that's assuming I get permission first.[ref:saitou-psycho]

sections.heading: WHEN WILL INVINCIBLE, MOSTLY A KID WRAP UP?
sections.content:
Q: When will the finale of Just About Invincible, Mostly a Kid be serialized? Or, when will the print edition come out? I'm not trying to rush you, I'm just curious about the ending. And, if it's not too much trouble, I'd love to see something like a mixer between the protagonists.

A: I can't make any firm promises, but I think it'll come out next year. As for the protagonists getting together — I think I'll write that later and put it up on the official site. Though it's just a bunch of stinky men, so I'm not sure there's much charm to it.[ref:shinshun-questionnaire]

sections.heading: NOT AN IDOL
sections.content:
Q: Iruma Hitoma-sensei! Why not start a fan club? The name, of course, would be: the Iruma Legion!

A: Ha ha ha, I'm not an idol, so unfortunately I won't be doing anything like that.

sections.heading: MORE POISON LIKE THE ONLY WISH?
sections.content:
Q: I have a question — do you plan to write more works with the kind of poison The Only Wish had? I really loved that book. Also, do you have any manga or games you'd recommend?

A: Even without deliberately steering myself in that direction, I'll probably end up writing something like that anyway — I hope you'll look forward to it when I do. As for a game — how about the recent Dragon's Crown? It's a lot of fun.[ref:dragons-crown]

sections.heading: DOES IRUMA KNOW ANY KILLERS?
sections.content:
Q: Killers show up pretty often in Iruma-sensei's work — don't tell me you actually know a few personally?

A: I don't even have friends — how on earth would I know any killers!

sections.heading: THE SECRET TO PALE SKIN
sections.content:
Q: People probably assume you're recuperating from an illness somewhere because your skin is so pale, so please tell us your secret to good skin.

A: My skin is… no, definitely not that. It's just weird.

sections.heading: A COSPLAY PHOTOBOOK?
sections.content:
Q: Isn't there a photobook of Iruma-sensei yet? Personally I think cosplaying as your own characters would be great — Hanasaki Tarou, the Futon Roll Monster, Shirasagi (with wings), that sort of thing would be wonderful.

A: Please don't tease me like that, I'll cry.[ref:futon-roll-photo]

sections.heading: COLLECTING THE LIAR, BROKEN SHORT STORIES
sections.content:
Q: I love Liar, Broken the most! So please, publish the Liar, Broken short stories from Dengeki Bunko MAGAZINE and the web novel in a print collection!

A: There's not quite enough material for a print collection yet. And I can't really think of enough new content to pad it out with, either.

sections.heading: A BREATHABLE FUTON FOR COSPLAY
sections.content:
Q: Now that we're heading into the hot season, could you recommend a nice, breathable blanket for cosplaying as the Futon Roll Monster in?

A: Please don't do that sort of thing in summer. Actually, don't do it too often in winter either — you'll trip over your own feet.

sections.heading: ONE EYE AND HEARTBREAK'S NEW TITLE
sections.content:
Q: Is One Eye and Heartbreak (tentative) not going to be released after all?

A: It'll be out in September. The title's been changed.[ref:hitomi-title]

sections.heading: SHOULD I DROP OUT TO BECOME A WRITER?
sections.content:
Q: I'm currently a second-year in high school, but I've already stopped attending. I want to drop out and aim to become a writer. Is being a novelist fun?

A: Work is, at its core, an unfun thing. I myself became a novelist partly to escape from having nothing to do, so I won't sit here and condemn you for wanting to escape — but personally, I think it's better to stay in school while you still can. I don't know the full details of your situation, so I won't push you one way or the other, but I don't think the odds are great that you'll run into something more fun than being a high schooler once that chapter is over. Isn't the back half of your teens basically the peak of life?

sections.heading: WHAT WAS IRUMA DOING AT TWENTY?
sections.content:
Q: What was Iruma Hitoma-sensei doing at age twenty?

A: I actually made it to the final round of some novel award — and then lost. Tch.

sections.heading: A SUPER-MYSTERIOUS VERSION?
sections.content:
Q: Aside from the SF version — where "SF" stands for "a little bit mysterious" — any chance of a super-mysterious version coming out?

A: I can't come up with anything super-mysterious, so probably not.

sections.heading: MORE AKKYUN AND MA-CHAN, PLEASE
sections.content:
Q: Please, I'm begging you — write a sequel to Akkyun and Ma-chan's daughter's story! I'm seriously low on Akkyun lately!

A: I'll — I'll write it soon… please hold on a little longer.

sections.heading: MARRY ME (I'M A HIGH SCHOOL SENIOR)
sections.content:
Q: Also, even though I'm only a high school senior — please marry me, with an eye toward us dating first!!

A: When you're proposing to Ludman, maybe give it a little more thought first.[ref:dq5-ludman]

sections.heading: DOES IRUMA USE TWITTER?
sections.content:
Q: Does Iruma-sensei use Twitter? There's someone on Twitter using Iruma-sensei's name, but they never say anything…

A: "Author So-and-so is once again spouting nonsense based on prejudice and delusion!" — that's the kind of headline that would probably end up with my name attached to it, so I've decided not to use Twitter. I think it's best if people whose character and conduct are questionable don't have a platform where they can broadcast to the world without going through anyone else. If people who see those kinds of posts end up thinking "oh, so this is what novelists are like," it'll cause trouble for the rest of us in the profession. By the way — that Twitter account isn't actually me.

sections.heading: IS THE YESTERDAY/TOMORROW DUOLOGY FINISHED?
sections.content:
Q: Are He Once Loved Her Yesterday and He'll Love Her Again Tomorrow still unfinished?

A: They're finished. Though, if you subscribe to the idea that "even after the final volume of a manga is published, the characters' lives keep going," then I suppose you could argue it's never really finished.

sections.heading: WHEN WILL THE ISOLATED GET A PRINT RELEASE?
sections.content:
Q: Any plans to release the print edition of The Isolated? I've been waiting, you know… is a print release planned?[ref:koritsusha]

A: It's scheduled for next year. Uki-sensei seems to be quite busy, so it'll probably end up on whatever timeline works around his schedule.

sections.heading: MEETING IRUMA AT A SPITZ CONCERT?
sections.content:
Q: You mentioned in Tamako and the Yellow Chicken that you like Spitz — so if I go to a Spitz concert, might I run into Iruma-sensei there?[ref:spitz]

A: You think I'd go somewhere that bright and cheerful?

sections.heading: STILL WAITING ON ONE EYE AND HEARTBREAK
sections.content:
Q: Is One Eye and Heartbreak really not coming out?

A: It is. Ah, well — not under that title anymore, that one's done for, but I've put together a short-story collection under the title The Thing Your Eyes Were Searching For, coming this September, please look forward to it.

sections.heading: STILL WRITING FOR MEDIAWORKS BUNKO?
sections.content:
Q: A question for Iruma-sensei! Have you stopped writing for MediaWorks Bunko? If not, when's the next release?

A: A short-story collection comes out in September. And there are plans for one more release before the year's out.

sections.heading: ADVICE, FAVORITE CHARACTERS, AND REWRITING LIVE A LIVE
sections.content:
Q: Please tell me the things I should study, the skills I should master, the things I should absolutely never do, and the things I should always keep in mind when writing a novel! Among characters from manga, novels, or anime, who is your favorite — the character you look at and think, "I want to live like that"? What kind of stories do you think readers are looking for? In an earlier afterword you said you wanted to "rewrite the novelization of LIVE A LIVE" — specifically, what parts would you want to rewrite?[ref:live-a-live]

A: Things to study when writing a novel… I'd love to know that myself, honestly. But if there's one thing you absolutely shouldn't do, it's outright plagiarism. Also — while a sense of realism does matter, don't misunderstand what that actually means. The realism of a work isn't about imitating reality; it's about making the story something the reader can accept and believe in. Even if it isn't realistic at all, if you can get the reader to instinctively think "I buy this!" — that's what matters. As for a character I admire — basically, I have a soft spot for rich characters. Wouldn't it be nice to live without having to work? As for what readers are looking for… I'd love to know that myself! I want to become more popular! And as for the novelization of LIVE A LIVE — the whole thing. I'd want to rewrite it completely from scratch. And if I'm allowed to be greedy about it, I'd want to novelize all the other chapters too.

sections.heading: ENSEMBLE DRAMAS AND MACHI
sections.content:
Q: What kind of novels do you enjoy writing most?

A: I love ensemble dramas the most. Especially the kind of structure you see in Machi.[ref:machi] Though its specific format — where seemingly unrelated storylines converge at the end — is a little different from what I usually do.

sections.heading: WHY NOT PUBLISH THE WEB NOVELS?
sections.content:
Q: I've basically read all of your standalone books, but I haven't read the web novels. Are there no plans to put those out in print?

A: Well — if you sent in a question through the site, that means you already know how to find the website… you're already here, so why not just read them?

sections.heading: HOW MANY VOLUMES UNTIL THE LIZARD KING ENDS?
sections.content:
Q: I honestly can't picture how The Lizard King is going to develop or how it'll end — roughly which volume are you planning to wrap it up in?

A: I already know how it ends, but I haven't decided which volume it'll actually conclude in.

sections.heading: RECENT FAVORITE AUTHORS
sections.content:
Q: I'd like to know which authors Iruma-sensei likes most recently. If possible, please name a few.

A: I honestly haven't read any novels lately… but there are plenty of manga artists I could name.

sections.heading: A NICKNAME FOR THE LIZARD KING?
sections.content:
Q: Simple question: does The Lizard King have a nickname? Saying something like "Look at that, the latest volume of Lizard!" makes it sound like you're talking about an animal encyclopedia. Could Sensei think one up? The one I came up with myself is Toka King — how's that?

A: I usually just call it "Lizard" myself. "Toka King" has kind of a Nidoking / Kamoking / Elecking vibe to it — it reads more like an actual name than an abbreviation, so something a bit shorter might be easier to say.[ref:pop-culture-kings]

sections.heading: THE ALUMINUM ALLOY MASTER
sections.content:
Q: Volume 5 of The Lizard King has a new character who carries an aluminum-alloy briefcase, and it moved me deeply. Combined with Dragonfly, you're basically an aluminum-alloy master at this point. I want to become an aluminum-alloy user too. Please let me become your disciple, Iruma-style.

A: For what it's worth, I originally misspelled it as "Jeruminium" at first. Wahahaha… gehhh.

sections.heading: PUBLISH THE WEB SHORT STORIES?
sections.content:
Q: By the way, I'd love it if all the novels you've published on the website so far got a print release as a short-story collection!

A: The content's pretty scattered, and some of it's still unfinished, so that'd be tough… They were all things I wrote with the mindset of "let people read this for free online" to begin with.

sections.heading: STILL WAITING ON THE PRINT RELEASE
sections.content:
Q: Still no print release for The Isolated~?[ref:koritsusha]

A: Not ye—et. (Please wait until next year. There are plans to include newly written content.)

sections.heading: MARRY ME, GENDER AND AGE ASIDE
sections.content:
Q: Please marry me!!!! I love you more than anyone else in the whole world!!!!!!! Gender doesn't matter! Age doesn't matter! Where there's love, nothing can stop us!! Once we're married, let's take on the world together!!

A: Men basically just want to be alone with their own two hands — I've always wanted to say that line once, inspired by a certain food manga.[ref:solitary-gourmet]

sections.heading: THE LIZARD KING'S ORIGIN, JOJO, AND PRETTY CURE
sections.content:
Q: What was the trigger for starting to write The Lizard King? What impact did watching the anime adaptation of Electric Girl and Adolescent Boy have on you? Iruma-sensei is famous for not writing outlines — what's the reasoning behind that? Of all the parts of JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, which is your favorite? Which Stand would you most want to have? Is there anything that makes you jealous of someone else's talent? Who's your favorite Pretty Cure?

A: The Lizard King came from wondering "what would happen if I tried writing something like a battle manga?" As for the Electric Girl anime — the anime started airing right around when the original novel wrapped up, so it didn't really influence anything. The whole "no outline" thing is really just because I'm bad at long-term planning — I'm terrible at shogi too, for the same reason. As for JoJo, my favorite part is Part 1. I really love the scene where Jonathan watches Dio dissolve and disappear, crying.[ref:jojo-part1] Looking at individual chapters, I also love the ending section of Part 5 with the Sleeping Slaves,[ref:jojo-part5] and — this might be a bit of a stretch to count — Deadman's Q is also great.[ref:deadmans-q] As for the Stand — Catch the Rainbow.[ref:catch-the-rainbow] As for talent — there's nothing in particular I'm jealous of. And Pretty Cure… "huh, are there really that many Pretty Cure shows?" I thought, and looked it up — turns out there really are a ton of them now. Since I've never watched a single one, I can't really pick a favorite, sorry.

sections.heading: I WANT TO BE KILLED BY MA-CHAN
sections.content:
Q: By the way, I want to be killed by Ma-chan. Reading Liar, Broken made me want to become a 2D character for the first time in my life. Please take responsibility for that.

A: I can't really take responsibility for that, but please do take care of your life. Who knows — maybe you'll actually figure out a way, decades from now.

sections.heading: FIRST CONTACT WITH ALIENS
sections.content:
Q: (eyes wide, gleaming) If you made first contact with aliens, what's the first thing you'd say?

A: I don't taste good.

sections.heading: IS IRUMA A SHOUNEN JUMP FAN?
sections.content:
Q: Sensei, I read your Q&A sessions, and I noticed you mentioned people you personally follow with interest. So — sensei, could it be that you're a fan of Shounen Jump?

A: I've been reading it for over twenty years. That said, back in the day I basically only read things like Dragon Ball. I remember the first time I read Jump when JoJo was running near the very front of the magazine — Koichi's hand had been turned to paper and rolled up.[ref:jojo-koichi] At the time I thought it was a horror manga and it scared me.

sections.heading: COME TO THE GUJO ODORI
sections.content:
Q: I live in Gujo City, where does Iruma-sensei live? Come see the Gujo Odori — it's a lot of fun.[ref:gujo-odori]

A: Do I look like the kind of person who'd go somewhere that bright and cheerful?

sections.heading: THE HARD PARTS AND THE FUN PARTS
sections.content:
Q: Nice to meet you! I'm just an ordinary person who likes The Lizard King and Electric Girl. 1. Are there hard parts or fun parts to writing a novel? 2. What's essential for writing a novel? 3. What keeps you going while you write?

A: 1. It's fun when people say a finished work was interesting — but everything up until it's finished is hard. 2. Firm, positive resolve to just die if you haven't finished by the deadline you set. 3. The hopeful future vision of "I'll build myself a royalty palace!" (which will probably never actually get built).

sections.heading: MOE OR GROTESQUE?
sections.content:
Q: Does Iruma-sensei prefer moe, like Electric Girl, or grotesque, like Liar, Broken and The Lizard King?

A: If it's interesting, I don't really care about genre. I think of novels as entertainment, first and foremost.

sections.heading: DOES IRUMA LIKE TOMATOES?
sections.content:
Q: Does Iruma-sensei like tomatoes!?

A: I eat them every day. The Maxim kind.[ref:maxim-tomato] Though it doesn't quite energize me to that degree.

sections.heading: WHAT'S IRUMA WRITING RIGHT NOW?
sections.content:
Q: I find myself wondering, from time to time, what novel Iruma-sensei is currently writing. I'd love to read a brand-new story showing off the unique world you create.

A: Since it might just end up scrapped, I'll keep it under wraps — but there are various sequels in the works. I want to squeeze in a new original work somewhere in between, too.

sections.heading: WHAT DOES THE LEGION ACTUALLY DO?
sections.content:
Q: What does the Iruma Legion actually do? You went and started this without even bringing me along — let me join too!

A: Nothing. Joining is totally fine, but… nothing at all, seriously — is that really okay with you?

sections.heading: KENDO CLUB AND A TIME-TRAVEL STORY
sections.content:
Q: Was Iruma-sensei in the kendo club back in high school? A lot of your characters talk about it, so I've been curious. Also, I'd love to read a story from you that deals with time, something in the vein of He Once Loved Her Yesterday and He'll Love Her Again Tomorrow.

A: I barely participated in any club activities in high school. As for a time-related story, I've got some ideas brewing, so please wait a bit longer. What I'm working on right now, actually, is a story about a girl who's going to die of illness in three years, and the effort to turn her into a fully healthy, muscle-bound person before then.[ref:small-scale-suicide]

sections.heading: HOW TO BUILD A RICHER VOCABULARY
sections.content:
Q: I write novels too, more or less as a hobby, but I've noticed my vocabulary is pretty limited. Iruma-sensei seems to have such a rich vocabulary — how can I build up my language skills the way you have?

A: More than vocabulary, what matters most in a novel is being able to accurately convey scenery and situations. It's not that using all kinds of fancy words automatically makes a novel interesting. That said, this is basically just my excuse for having a limited vocabulary myself.

sections.heading: STILL REMEMBERING SIX GUNS, SIX PEOPLE, SIX DAYS
sections.content:
Q: Speaking of which, Iruma-sensei, it's been almost a year since the first volume of Six Guns, Six People, Six Days came out — you haven't forgotten about it, have you?

A: I do still remember that this thing exists, but I've completely forgotten what the story was actually about, so I'm currently rereading it myself.

sections.heading: BIG OR SMALL?
sections.content:
Q: Does Iruma-sensei prefer big chests or small chests? I like small chests myself!

A: As the old saying goes, the greater can always substitute for the lesser.[ref:size-proverb]

sections.heading: A FAVORITE KANJI
sections.content:
Q: I love Iruma Hitoma-sensei's stories the most. What's your favorite kanji character?

A: 夢 (Dream).

sections.heading: SUMMER BREAK ACTIVITIES
sections.content:
Q: College summer breaks are so long… What does Iruma-sensei do to burn through all that extra free time?

A: I spend it playing video games, obviously — and I write a lot of novels too.

references.title: The Isolated (Koritsusha)
references.note: The Isolated is a novel whose chapter titles are a numbered countdown of days (accounting correctly for leap years) toward a particular point in the story. We were unable to conclusively verify this title's official Japanese name, publisher, or illustrator (referred to elsewhere in this Q&A as "Uki-sensei," likely the illustrator Atsuya Uki, one of Iruma's regular collaborators) from available records, and have left the specific identification open pending further sourcing.

references.title: "Multiple Personality, Roughly Saitou"
references.note: In a prior afterword, Iruma described an unpublished submission with this premise: seven aliens invade Earth intending to each possess a different human, but all seven accidentally end up sharing the same body, that of an unlucky man named Saitou, forcing them to take turns controlling him while another parasitic alien species begins invading Earth in the meantime. Iruma titled this manuscript "Multiple Personality, Roughly Saitou."

references.title: The Multiple Personality Detective Psycho Pun
references.note: The title "Multiple Personality, Roughly Saitou" is a play on Multiple Personality Detective Psycho (Tajuu Jinkaku Tantei Saiko), a manga by Eiji Otsuka and Shou Tajima. Iruma's comment about needing "permission" refers to this echo of an existing, unrelated title.

references.title: The Protagonist Get-Together, Realized
references.note: The following January, Iruma made good on this answer, publishing a short story bringing together the protagonists of his various series, titled "New Year's Protagonist Survey." Because Adachi and Shimamura were included among the cast, the final result ended up being more than "just a bunch of stinky men" as Iruma jokingly worried here.

references.title: Dragon's Crown
references.note: Dragon's Crown is a 2D side-scrolling action RPG developed by Vanillaware and published by Atlus, released in Japan on July 25, 2013 — about a month before this Q&A was posted.

references.title: Iruma's Futon Roll Monster Cosplay
references.note: Iruma Hitoma has in fact dressed up as the "Futon Roll Monster" (a recurring joke creature in his work) before, appearing in the author bio section of Volume 2 of Electric Girl and Adolescent Boy alongside the caption "I heard that a sense of reality is the energy that gives a work life…"

references.title: One Eye and Heartbreak's Title Change
references.note: One Eye and Heartbreak was originally scheduled for a January 2012 release, but ultimately came out in September 2013 under the new title The Thing Your Eyes Were Searching For. A magazine short story originally intended for inclusion, "The Sky Falls Because of Eyes," was left out due to editorial concerns and was instead published in full on the official website in August 2012.

references.title: Ludman's Proposal Scene
references.note: In Dragon Quest V, if the player speaks to Ludman — father of one of the potential brides, Flora — during the marriage-proposal sequence, he responds: "What? You're saying you like me?! Th-that won't do at all! You should give it some more thought." Iruma redirects this line back at the questioner.

references.title: LIVE A LIVE and Iruma's Spin-Off Short Story
references.note: LIVE A LIVE is an RPG released by Square in 1994, structured as eight chapters set in different eras with different protagonists, plus a linking finale. Iruma previously wrote an official spin-off short story for the game's science-fiction chapter, titled "Kore Omou Yueni Ware Ari——," published in the November 2008 supplementary issue of Dengeki Bunko MAGAZINE.

references.title: Machi
references.note: Machi ~Unmei no Kousaten~ is a 1998 live-action adventure game by Chunsoft, built around several seemingly unconnected character storylines that intersect and converge by the end — the kind of ensemble structure Iruma cites as a formative influence.

references.title: Nidoking, Kamoking, and Elecking
references.note: Nidoking is a Pokémon species introduced in the original Pokémon Red and Green. Elecking is a recurring kaiju from the Ultra Series, first appearing in Ultraman Seven. Kamoking is a monster from the 1997 Square RPG Saga Frontier. Iruma lists all three as examples of why "Toka King" reads more like a proper name than a nickname.

references.title: The Solitary Gourmet Quote
references.note: Iruma's line paraphrases a piece of narration from Episode 2 of the original Kodoku no Gurume (Solitary Gourmet) manga: "Men basically want to remain a single body" — used here as a lighthearted deflection of the marriage proposal.

references.title: The Ending of JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 1
references.note: At the climax of Phantom Blood (Part 1), Dio Brando's body is destroyed by sunlight aboard a burning ship. As he dies from Dio's poison alongside him, Jonathan Joestar recalls their shared childhood and sheds a tear — the scene Iruma cites as his favorite.

references.title: The "Sleeping Slaves" Epilogue of Part 5
references.note: "Sleeping Slaves" is the title of the final chapter of Vento Aureo (Part 5), an epilogue in which the sculptor Scolippi reflects on whether Bucciarati and his allies were fated to die, or whether they were "sleeping slaves" who broke free of destiny through their own will.

references.title: Deadman's Q
references.note: Deadman's Q is a short spin-off manga by Hirohiko Araki set after the events of Diamond Is Unbreakable (Part 4), starring Yoshikage Kira as a memory-loss ghost. Volume 2, Chapter 2 of Adachi and Shimamura, titled "Adachi Q," takes its name from this story.

references.title: Catch the Rainbow
references.note: Catch the Rainbow is the Stand belonging to the character Blackmore in Steel Ball Run (Part 7) of JoJo's Bizarre Adventure.

references.title: Koichi's Paper Hand
references.note: Iruma is recalling an early scene from Diamond Is Unbreakable (Part 4), in which Koichi Hirose's hand is transformed into paper and rolled up by an enemy Stand user — one of Iruma's first exposures to the series.

references.title: Gujo Odori
references.note: Gujo Odori is a centuries-old Bon Festival dance held over dozens of nights each summer in the Gujo Hachiman district of Gujo City, Gifu Prefecture — coincidentally Iruma's home prefecture, though not his hometown.

references.title: Maxim Tomato
references.note: The Maxim Tomato is a recurring item in the Kirby video game series that fully restores the player's health when eaten.

references.title: My Small-Scale Suicide
references.note: The story concept Iruma describes here — a terminally ill girl being pushed toward physical health before her prognosis catches up with her — became the novel My Small-Scale Suicide, released in December 2013.

references.title: "The Greater Can Substitute for the Lesser"
references.note: A Japanese proverb (dai wa shou wo kaneru), roughly equivalent to "the bigger option covers the smaller one too," used here as a noncommittal, joking non-answer.

references.title: Spitz
references.note: Spitz is a long-running Japanese rock band, formed in 1987 and best known for hits like "Robinson" and "Cherry." Iruma name-drops them as a favorite in his short story Tamako and the Yellow Chicken.
